submissions.findingTextShort: Five randomized placebo-controlled trials support anxiety-symptom benefit for proprietary oral Silexan, not lavender products generally.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A meta-analysis of five completed double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trials involving 1,213 adult outpatients found anxiety-symptom and global-improvement signals with proprietary oral Silexan 80 mg once daily for 10 weeks; the evidence belongs to this standardized Lavandula angustifolia oil preparation and must not be generalized to tea, generic capsules, topical oil, aromatherapy, or every essential-oil product.
submissions.populationContext: Adult outpatients with subthreshold anxiety, mixed anxiety/depressive disorder, or generalized anxiety disorder
submissions.usageContext: Proprietary oral Silexan 80 mg once daily for 10 weeks
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Product/developer affiliation with Dr. Willmar Schwabe GmbH & Co. KG must remain visible in provenance review.

submissions.findingTextShort: Broader lavender anxiety evidence spans multiple routes and has substantial quality and heterogeneity limitations.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A 2019 systematic review and meta-analysis covering 65 randomized trials and 25 nonrandomized studies qualitatively, with 37 randomized trials in quantitative synthesis, reported anxiety signals across inhalation and oral Silexan contexts but highlighted low average study quality, high risk of bias in many randomized trials, and major heterogeneity especially for non-oral administration; this prevents route-agnostic class-wide certainty.
submissions.usageContext: Multiple lavender preparations and administration routes
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Broader route-level synthesis should calibrate, not erase, the more specific Silexan randomized evidence.

submissions.findingTextShort: A 2026 meta-analysis found a sleep-quality signal from lavender essential-oil interventions, with evidence-quality limitations.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis of 11 randomized trials involving 628 adults found an average sleep-quality improvement with lavender essential-oil interventions, while the authors cautioned that the number and quality of included studies constrain confidence; this sleep evidence is separate from oral Silexan anxiety evidence and must retain route and preparation details.
submissions.usageContext: Lavender essential-oil sleep interventions across heterogeneous protocols
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Do not infer one universal lavender sleep regimen or transfer Silexan dosing into this evidence domain.

submissions.findingTextShort: Older-adult inhalation studies show a sizable pooled sleep signal but very high heterogeneity.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A 2025 systematic review and meta-analysis of lavender for sleep disorders in adults older than 60 years found a sizable pooled sleep-quality signal in studies using inhalation, but heterogeneity was very high at I-squared 87.5 percent; the result is therefore population- and route-specific and should be presented as heterogeneous rather than uniformly established efficacy.
submissions.populationContext: Adults older than 60 years with sleep-disorder outcomes
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Very high heterogeneity prevents a single expected effect size or universal inhalation protocol.
